_why_this_file_exists: four of the scripts that produced these numbers print them and write no file (validate.py, round3.py, lang.py, zhconfirm.py), so the figures survived only in that session's transcript; this file is the persisted copy

operating_point.ask: q6 — "Do you need to do something about this message? Answer act or ignore."
operating_point.accuracy_at_this_cut_note: corrected 2026-10-25. This field said 1.0, which was the best cut's accuracy recorded as though it were this cut's. At 0.600 four act cases read 0.3948, 0.3956, 0.4074 and 0.5318, so 20 of 24 are correct. Re-derived from the per-case probabilities in calibration/vision/server-transport.json, which agree with the one-shot rig to 0.0003 per case and give the same 20/24. AUC is 1.000 and the two classes separate perfectly, so a cut in (0.3845, 0.3948] scores 24/24 — but 0.600 is not in that interval, and the threshold is unmoved: moving it is the host's word (docs/decisions.md row 12), not a correction's.
operating_point.how: validate.py swept thresholds in steps of 0.025 over 1/40..39/40 and reported the best, on a set written after every prompt choice had been made. Corrected 2026-10-25: this said 0.600 is that best, and it is not. On that grid the best is 23/24, at 0.35, 0.375 or 0.4; 0.600 earns 20/24. The grid cannot land inside the separating interval (0.3845, 0.3948] at all, because its points step over it — a 0.025 sweep on 24 cases is too coarse to find the cut these cases actually have, which is why the interval above matters more than the grid's best

how_the_probability_was_read._load_bearing: the measurement and the runtime read one estimator, and this file records which one — corrected 2026-10-25, when it said they did not
how_the_probability_was_read.measurement: vocab.py built a map keyed by the tokeniser's decoded text with .strip().lower(), so ids_for('act') returns every id whose decoding strips to 'act' — six of them for this checkpoint (598, 901, 3619, 7372, 15674, 32234). P(act) was the sum over all of them, and P(ignore) likewise, normalised over the pair.
how_the_probability_was_read.runtime: llama.ts readingOf reads that same quantity: it sums exp(logprob) over every candidate whose decoded form strips to the option, and src/llama.test.ts asserts the sum rather than leaving it to a comment. Corrected 2026-10-25 — this said the runtime "masks that single id", with bindOptions named as the reader, and that is not what it does. bindOptions still measures one id per option, but that id is the position the answer is read at, not the quantity read there: agent-lifecycle.md §4 line 79's single-token rule is about the option surviving as one token, which both readings require, and it never said to read one id's probability alone.
how_the_probability_was_read.consequence: the cut was chosen and is applied under one estimator, so the number means what it was measured to mean. Corrected 2026-10-25 — this called the difference a "stated open tension": docs/decisions.md row 19 has since settled it the other way, and calibration/vision/server-transport.json replays the summed reading through the transport the runtime actually uses, reproducing this file's set (AUC 1.000, 20/24 at 0.600, per-case difference at most 0.0008). It is still why a replacement model must clear the same measurement before it ships: a number is only meaningful together with the way it was read.
how_the_probability_was_read.normalisation_not_yet_checkable: One difference between the two descriptions is not settled and is not claimed settled here: vocab.py normalised P(act) over the pair (act against ignore), while readingOf returns the raw sum, and calibration/vision/server-transport.json's shape.answer_read describes the raw sum too. So either the normalisation moves these cases by less than the 0.0008 that transport already reproduces, or the recorded set and the replay are both un-normalised and the sentence in 'measurement' describes arithmetic only vocab.py performed. Nothing in the tree can tell the two apart, because no per-case pre-normalisation value was written down. Settling it needs one run of the text set recording the raw act and ignore sums per case; until then the cut is applied to the raw sum and the agreement figure above stands on its own measurement rather than on this sentence.

what_was_not_measured: vision is measured, not unmeasured: 56 English image cases and 12 Chinese in calibration/vision/, read 2026-10-25 — 41/56 at the shipped 0.600, 48/56 at a cut near 0.39, and at most 8/12 on the Chinese at any cut. The requirement stands unmet for a narrower reason than this entry used to give: the Chinese shortfall is the model's discrimination, which no operating point repairs.
